summary: investigate further: the paper's six-month momentum strategy, adapted here to a long-only top-decile portfolio drawn from 415 current S&P 500 names, earned a net CAGR of 14.54% against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe, with Sharpe 0.68 against 0.65. The edge is not robust: it fails at 10 bps of cost, holds in 0 of 2 sub-periods, the ten groups do not rank in the expected direction (rho -0.28), and the alpha t-statistic is 0.32. The Monte Carlo economics are positive, with P(NPV > 0) 76% and a median incremental fee PV of $2.0M against the equal-weight fund, but this rests on an assumed 2/20 fee schedule with a hard hurdle. The test uses a survivor universe, is long-only, and lies entirely after publication. The recommendation is to investigate further because performance and economics are positive while robustness is weak.

sections.What the paper proposes: Jegadeesh and Titman (1999) test whether momentum profits come from a risk premium or from delayed reaction to information. The experiment we selected is Table 1: stocks are ranked at the end of each month on their past six-month return, grouped into ten equal-weighted decile portfolios, and each is held for six months in overlapping monthly cohorts, with no skip month. The paper reports that past winners (P1) beat past losers (P10) by 1.11% per month (t-statistic 4.61) over 1965-1989, 1.01% per month (t 4.10) over 1990-1997, and 1.09% per month (t 5.65) over 1965-1997. The authors read this as support for behavioral delayed-overreaction models.
sections.What we implemented and changed: We ranked on the cumulative six-month return with no skip, formed equal-count deciles, held each cohort for 6 months with monthly rebalancing, and weighted equally, all as the paper states. The changes are listed plainly. We hold only the highest group, so there is no short leg. The universe is 415 names from our S&P 500 snapshot, eligible from their index add date; 19 names were excluded for missing Yahoo data. Deciles are equal-count sorts of eligible names, with no exchange or size breakpoints. The paper's $5 price floor was not applied, because the snapshot's prices are split-adjusted rather than as-traded and a dollar floor would drop the wrong names. The sample runs from 2015-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (warm-up from 2012-01-01) over 132 monthly formation dates, with transaction costs of 10 bps. Two fields were assumed because the paper is silent: 252 days of history to be eligible and 15 trading days minimum in a formation month. In total 2 fields were assumed, 5 were adapted, and 13 details the paper leaves open were handled by engine defaults, including the return compounding convention, delisting returns, and whether cohort weights drift or reset.
sections.What the backtest found: The strategy earned a net CAGR of 14.54% against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe, and Sharpe 0.68 against 0.65. SPY returned a CAGR of 0.13453 with Sharpe 0.686041, so the strategy's Sharpe is slightly below SPY's. The excess CAGR over the equal-weight universe is 0.018315, but the Newey-West t-statistic on the monthly difference is 1.09607, which is not significant. Net maximum drawdown was -0.342222 and mean monthly turnover was 0.151131. The evidence for a momentum premium is weak. The alpha t-statistic is 0.32 against the Fama-French factors plus momentum, and -0.170382 in the spanning regression. The edge over the equal-weight universe fails at 10 bps, and the alpha t-statistic at 25 bps is -0.020555. It holds in 0 of 2 sub-periods. Across the ten groups, the rank correlation is -0.284848 (p-value 0.425038), which is not in the expected direction. Group 10 earned a mean monthly return of 0.012455 and group 1 earned 0.012654, a difference of -0.000199 with a t-statistic of -0.06847. The favored group did not beat the disfavored group, unlike the paper's long-short result.
sections.What the simulation and economics found: We resampled historical days in geometric blocks (mean block length 126 days) for 1000 paths over a 5-year horizon, using a fund charged 2/20 with a 5% hard hurdle and a high-water mark. That fee schedule is an assumption, not an observed one. Incremental fees are measured against an equal-weight universe fund charged the same fees, never against SPY. P(NPV > 0) is 76%, and the median incremental fee PV is $2.0M. The strategy beat the equal-weight universe fund in 0.763 of paths but beat SPY in only 0.111. When the historical mean excess return over the equal-weight fund is removed, the share of paths with positive NPV falls to 0.477, so the positive result depends on the historical excess return persisting. Across block lengths of 63, 126 and 252 days the share beating the equal-weight fund was 0.723333, 0.766667 and 0.793333. The bootstrap cannot create regimes absent from the sample. On capacity, none of the 13938 trades exceeded 10% of average daily volume at the assumed starting fund size.
sections.How reliable the interpretation was: Implementation reliability is green: evidence quotes were valid for 100% of the 16 fields checked, and there were 0 critical check disagreements. Across 2 extraction runs, mean field agreement was 0.944444, with the lowest agreement of 0.5 on economic_rationale and rebalance_frequency. Scored against a preliminary reference, agreement was 0.357143 over 14 compared fields, with 3 critical errors (signal_formula_words, holding_period, favored_group) and 6 minor errors. That reference is itself preliminary, so the score should be read with that caveat, but the mismatches are real differences in how the fields were written and are not resolved. The 13 unresolved details mean some implementation choices rest on engine defaults rather than the paper.
sections.What to do next: The recommendation is to investigate further, not to pursue. The first priority is the survivor universe: rerun on point-in-time index membership including delisted names, since the current universe flatters returns. Second, test the paper's own design more closely with as-traded prices so the $5 floor can be applied, and add the short leg to compare against the paper's long-short spread. Third, extend the sample to periods before publication, because the 2015-2025 window lies entirely after it and shows no group ordering. Fourth, resolve the 13 unresolved details one at a time to see which change the result. Finally, finalize the interpretation reference so the agreement score is no longer measured against a preliminary one.
